steps.say: Urinary tuberculosis never starts in the urine: it rains down from the lungs through the blood. Mycobacterium tuberculosis escapes a pulmonary focus into the bloodstream and seeds the renal cortex, lodging in glomeruli and peritubular capillaries where oxygen runs rich. After years of silent granulomas, the kidney is unmasked by sterile pyuria that no ordinary antibiotic touches.
steps.tx: Trace **genitourinary tuberculosis** (**GUTB**, urinary TB) to hematogenous seeding: **Mycobacterium tuberculosis** (TB germ) spreads from a primary pulmonary focus to renal cortical glomeruli and peritubular capillaries. Cortical granulomas smoulder for years before ulcerating into tubules, so a past chest infection explains a present bladder complaint, and chest imaging belongs in every GUTB workup.

steps.say: The signature presentation is pus in the urine with nothing growing on plates, repeated again and again. Sterile pyuria, meaning white cells in urine with negative routine bacterial cultures, is the classic hallmark of urinary tuberculosis and should trigger mycobacterial testing on the spot. Ordinary cystitis never behaves this way, so the mismatch itself is the diagnosis knocking.
steps.tx: Chase **sterile pyuria** (white cells without bacterial growth) as the hallmark of **urinary tuberculosis** (TB of the urinary tract): leukocytes with repeatedly negative routine cultures demand mycobacterial smear, culture, and GeneXpert. Three early morning urine samples beat one random cup, because bacilli shed intermittently, and a positive test reroutes the patient from urology antibiotics to tuberculosis therapy.

steps.say: The ureter betrays tuberculosis with a beaded corkscrew no other disease makes. Transmural caseating granulomas stricture the tube at multiple levels, and contrast films show the Kerr kink: a stepladder or corkscrew ureter rigid with fibrosis. A pipe-stem ureter on imaging is tuberculosis until proven otherwise, even when the chest film looks clean.
steps.tx: Read the **Kerr kink** (beaded TB ureter): multi-segment strictures from transmural caseating granulomas draw a stepladder or **corkscrew ureter** (twisted rigid tube), the classic **pipe-stem ureter** (stiff narrow pipe) of urinary TB. Fibrosis fixes the kinks permanently, so stenting buys time but reconstruction follows cure, and bilateral kinks warn of global renal threat.

steps.say: The bladder can shrink to a thimble that holds barely a teacup of urine. Profound muscular scarring contracts the viscus to under 50 to 100 millilitres, and no drug re-expands dead muscle, so once medical cure is proven the bladder is surgically enlarged with a patch of bowel called enterocystoplasty. Frequency with tiny painful voids after treated TB is a surgical bladder, not more tablets.
steps.tx: Measure the end stage: **thimble bladder** (shrunken fibrotic bladder, **contracted bladder**) holds **<50 mL to 100 mL** (under fifty to one hundred millilitres) after muscular scarring, and needs **enterocystoplasty** (bowel patch bladder augmentation) once medical cure is verified. Augment only proven-cured bladders, because operating on active TB seeds the bowel patch and fails twice.

steps.say: A kidney can die so completely that it mummifies into chalk. Caseous necrosis with total calcification replaces the whole parenchyma, leaving a putty kidney, also called cement kidney: a dead autonephrectomy that neither makes urine nor merits saving. The dead organ still harbours live bacilli though, so symptomatic putty kidneys with pain or hypertension come out.
steps.tx: Name the end stage: **putty kidney** (**cement kidney**, calcified dead kidney) means complete **autonephrectomy** (self destroyed kidney) where caseous necrosis and calcification replace all parenchyma. The devitalized organ makes no urine yet shelters bacilli, so remove painful or hypertensive putty kidneys while leaving silent calcified ones watched, since dead tissue needs no drugs but live germs need respect.

steps.say: Urinary tuberculosis is cured with the same six month recipe as lung disease, and shortcuts breed resistance. The standard 6-month regimen gives two months of four drugs, isoniazid with rifampin plus pyrazinamide and ethambutol, then four months of isoniazid with rifampin alone. Directly observed doses protect the long tail, because stopping at symptomatic relief resurrects bacilli.
steps.tx: Prescribe the full **6-month regimen** (standard TB course) of **antitubercular therapy** (TB medicines): 2 months of **isoniazid**, **rifampin**, **pyrazinamide**, **ethambutol**, then 4 months of isoniazid with rifampin. Supervised DOTS dosing guards adherence across the symptom-free months, since truncated courses convert curable urinary TB into multidrug resistant disease.

vis.caption: DOTS antitubercular therapy: the supervised 6-month regimen cures GUTB. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Not every white ball in the kidney is a stone: in diabetics and the immunocompromised, fungus felts into obstructing bezoars. Candida albicans bezoars, or fungal balls, mat together in the renal pelvis and block urine like soft stones that scanners misread. Flank pain with fungal urine in a diabetic is a bezoar until a stone is proven, because the treatments diverge completely.
steps.tx: Suspect **fungal ball** (**Candida bezoar**, Candida albicans mats) obstruction in diabetic or immunocompromised hosts: felted masses plug the renal pelvis where stones would sit. **Candida** (thrush yeast) in urine with colicky pain and a soft filling defect marks bezoars, so send fungal cultures before booking stone surgery, since lasers cannot vaporize felt.

vis.alt: Microscopic view of Candida organisms responsible for fungal bezoars.
vis.caption: Candida microscopic view: fungal balls felt from the same yeast in diabetics. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Fungal bezoars demand plumbing plus poison: debulk the mass, wash the system, and treat the blood. Endourological or open debulking clears the bulk, continuous local irrigation with amphotericin B at 50 milligrams per litre sterilizes the pelvis, and systemic fluconazole chases tissue invasion. Skipping irrigation leaves rind that regrows, and skipping systemic drug misses invasion beyond the lumen.
steps.tx: Clear bezoars three ways: surgical or endourological debulking, continuous **amphotericin B irrigation** (pelvis wash, **50 mg/L**, fifty milligrams per litre, sterile water) plus systemic **fluconazole** (azole antifungal) therapy. Local wash sterilizes the lumen while systemic drug reaches invaded tissue, so combine all three arms and correct the diabetes or immune gap behind the bloom.
